title: Recollection Window Length and the Requisition Expiry Limit
content:
The recollection window for a rejected specimen on a Laboratory Test Orders accession is a whole number of calendar days. It is the class recollection window of the accession's service class, counted from the date of the most recent specimen rejection on the accession. The rejection date is day 0 and the last day is included.

## Requisition expiry limit

The recollection window granted never runs past the expiry of the requisition. It is limited to the class's requisition validity period less the calendar days from the order date to the rejection date. Where that remaining room is shorter than the window, the remaining room is the window granted.

## Worked examples (hypothetical class window of 10 days, hypothetical requisition validity of 60 days)

| Order date | Rejection date | Days from order date to rejection | Remaining room before requisition expiry | Window granted | Recollect-by date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 11 March | 10 | 50 | 10 | 21 March |
| 1 March | 25 April | 55 | 5 | 5 | 30 April |

In the first row the remaining room (50 days) is longer than the window, so the window stands at 10 days. In the second row the requisition would expire 5 days after the rejection, so the window granted is 5 days.

## Points of judgement

- **Which rejection does the clock start from?** The most recent specimen rejection on the accession.
- **Does the window run in business days?** No. It runs in calendar days, with the rejection date as day 0 and the last day included.
